topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Progression and Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks outline the lecture aims, review the multistep model of tumor progression, and introduce the cancer hallmarks framework.

topics.label: Deregulated Growth and Survival Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive autonomous proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how arrested terminal differentiation contributes to malignancy in both hematological and intestinal cancers.

topics.label: Evading Cell Death, Senescence, and p53-Mediated Stress Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells circumvent intrinsic fail-safe mechanisms including apoptosis, telomere-driven senescence, and p53 tumor suppressor activity.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming and Epigenetic Alterations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors alter cellular metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, metabolic enzyme mutations, and epigenetic feedback loops.

topics.label: Angiogenesis in Tumor Growth and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the physiological requirement, developmental timing, and regulatory balance of new blood vessel recruitment in tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Detection, and Genetics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the multi-step metastatic cascade, diagnostic tracking methods, and clonal genetic features associated with secondary tumor colonization.

topics.label: Conclusion and Final Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding section wraps up the lecture with summary observations on cancer hallmarks, recommended further reading, and practical session information.
